title: Mechanisms of insulin action and insulin resistance

result: Narrative review. INSR is a heterotetramer of two insulin-binding alpha subunits and two beta subunits with tyrosine kinase domains; trans-autophosphorylation of Tyr1162, Tyr1158 and Tyr1163 activates it, and it phosphorylates IRS1 and IRS2, which recruit PI3K (p85 regulatory, p110 catalytic). PIP3 recruits PDK1 and AKT, phosphorylated at Thr308 by PDK1 and at Ser473 by mTORC2. In primary human myotubes, knockdown of AKT2 but not AKT1 abrogated insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis; a partial loss-of-function AKT2 variant in about 1% of the Finnish population impairs insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and increases endogenous glucose production. AKT phosphorylation of TBC1D4 (AS160) blocks its inactivation of Rab GTPases and promotes GLUT4 storage-vesicle translocation, first reported in 1980; a truncating TBC1D4 mutation caused profound insulin resistance in one family. Glycogen synthesis accounts for about 75% of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal in human muscle; mice with GSK3 insensitive to insulin have normal insulin-stimulated glycogen synthesis, suggesting acute control mainly by glucose 6-phosphate allostery. Muscle stores energy mostly for its own use, releasing lactate and alanine. Hepatocyte glucose transport is not insulin-regulated; AKT phosphorylates FOXO1, excluding it from the nucleus and lowering G6pc and Pck1 transcription. Suppression of adipose lipolysis has an ED50 of about 20 µU/mL insulin, within a physiological range of about 5 to 60 µU/mL. Hepatic glycogen is nearly depleted after 48 h of fasting in humans, while gluconeogenic flux stays relatively constant for about 48 h. In rodents, acute insulin suppression of gluconeogenesis depends mainly on suppression of adipose lipolysis, hepatic acetyl-CoA and pyruvate carboxylase flux, and mice lacking hepatic AKT1, AKT2 and FOXO1 suppressed glucose production normally; the quantitative significance in humans remains to be explored. Insulin suppresses glucagon secretion through paracrine action in the islet.
